## Claimed + dispatched — the sibling convention is now on `main`

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`,
branch `claude/issue-6004-generatecolumns-typed`. All agents share one GitHub identity — **this
comment's session ID is the claim**, not the assignee.

### ⭐ Read #6373 first — it is the same defect shape, it just landed, and it wrote you a rule

#6373 applied this remedy to the **second** producer (`plugin-dashboard`'s `ObjectDataTable`
`enrich()`); it merged as PR #6427. Its criterion, which you should apply to **your** key set
rather than re-inventing:

> write only what the consumer reads; measure the consumer's read set from its source; never
> declare a key nothing reads; before retiring, prove the value has a second road to its consumer.

That last clause is what makes "retire" safe rather than lossy — each of its six retirements
carried a measured read-count of 0 **plus** the second road the value still travels.

### ⚠️⚠️ The obvious remedy is INERT here — this is the finding that PR paid for

The card (and this family's earlier framing) says "annotate the producer's return as
`TableColumn[]`". **That raises no error**: TypeScript's excess-property check **exempts properties
arriving through a spread**, so a `{ ...col, ...fieldMeta }`-style emit type-checks against a
`TableColumn[]` annotation while enforcing nothing. It is a blind instrument — green gate, no
guard.

What holds instead, landed at `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx`, is a derived
tombstone intersection that bites by **assignability**:

```ts
& { [K in Exclude<keyof FieldMeta, keyof TableColumn | 'name'>]?: never }
```

⭐ **Derived, never hand-listed** — a hand-written tombstone set goes stale the moment the source
type grows a key.

### ⚠️ Your surface is wider than #6373's, and the `any` casts are a second inert layer

Censused on `origin/main` `129c7a9e7`:

```
packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:1525  const generateColumns = useCallback(() => {
                                       :2108  generateColumns().filter((c: any) => …)
                                       :2176  generateColumns().filter((c: any) => …)
                                       :2227  generateColumns().map((col: any) => {
```

**Three consumers, and every one of them casts to `any`.** So even a tombstone-bearing return type
is defeated at the call site unless those casts go too. ⛔ Do not leave them: an emit type nothing
downstream honours is the same blind-instrument failure one hop later. If removing a cast surfaces
a real type error, that is a finding to report — not a reason to reinstate the cast.

⛔ Re-derive all of this yourself; these are my numbers on today's `main`.

### Adjudication boundaries

Each surfaced key gets **declare / retire / hold-as-alias** with a stated reason. ⛔ Do not make the
type-check pass by widening `TableColumn` with an index signature or a cast — that converts a
surfaced-key census into a silenced one, which is the failure this family exists to undo.

⛔ Keys already adjudicated elsewhere are not yours: **`type`** is #5853's (closed), **`name`** is
#5120's (open). If your key set overlaps #6424 / #6425 (filed off #6373), report the overlap rather
than folding them in.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read.** **(b) Shadow check** — in flight: #6038, #6416, and #6419
  (`plugin-view`) in the same batch; none touches `plugin-grid`. #6373 is **merged**, so
  `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` is free. **(c) Census** above.

### Ghost-assertion guard

The defect is type-level, so a test that merely renders the grid is **blind** — it stays green with
the annotation removed. Pin something the annotation's *absence* actually breaks, prove it red by
mutating to the pre-fix condition, restore by **hash**, and measure type-check coverage with
`tsc -p … --listFiles` rather than assuming a green gate covers your files.

Deliver a **draft** PR with `Fixes #6004`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not self-merge, ⛔ do not
enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

**ACCEPT** — both review items discharged, verified against the branch rather than the report. PR #6461, head `356d0d93a`.

### 1. Null guards — restored, and one of them is better than what I asked for

I asked for `if (!col || col.type == null) return col;` on the fold pass. The branch carries `if (!col) return col;` followed by `if (producerType == null) return rest;` after the destructure. I went looking for a missing limb and found the opposite: splitting it is the more correct shape. The single guard I specified would have returned `col` **with the producer-spelled `type` still attached** — and `type` is precisely the member whose vocabulary differs between `ObjectGridColumnDraft` and `ObjectGridColumn`. Returning `rest` strips it. My phrasing was the weaker one; the dev's split stands.

The enrichment guard at `:2407` matches the ask exactly, and both carry the five-`any` history in the comment, including the point that mattered — `const generatedColumns: any[]` was **inside** `generateColumns()` itself, so annotating the return had left a whole emit path unchecked.

### 2. The dist check was the right instinct

Both guards are unreachable *by type* — TS narrows `col` to `never` there — which is exactly the condition under which a bundler is entitled to delete them. Verifying they survive minification in `dist/index.js` rather than assuming it is the difference between defence in depth and a comment. That check was not asked for and should have been.

### 3. Gate discipline held where it was designed to fail

`git diff --stat origin/main...356d0d93a -- scripts/` is **empty**. The collision gate's failure message prints a ready-to-paste `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` entry one line below its own SHRINK-ONLY warning; taking it would have weakened the gate instead of satisfying it. The card was resolved by renaming, and `scripts/` carries no diff at all.

### 4. Rename — measured, not asserted

- `ObjectObjectGrid` — **0 occurrences**, so the pre-existing `ObjectGridColumnState` was not corrupted by the lookbehind.
- `ObjectGridColumnState` — **3 occurrences**, unchanged.
- The surviving bare `GridColumn` hits are `CHANGELOG.md` (history, correctly not rewritten) and `GridColumnAddress` in `columnSpellingDiagnostics.ts` — a different symbol, correctly left alone.

### 5. Clause-② — no public surface change, and this is measured

The report did not state this, so I measured it: `git diff origin/main...356d0d93a -- packages/plugin-grid/src/index.tsx` is **empty**. `ObjectGridColumn`, `ObjectGridColumnDraft` and `ObjectGridColumnHolds` are file-level exports that the package entry never re-exports; the only column type on the published surface is `ObjectGridColumnState`, whose name did not move. So the rename cannot reach a consumer, and this stays at ordinary tier rather than contract-review.

Enqueue is held only on CI: 29 checks, **zero failed**, 5 pending (4 test shards + Type Check). It goes to the merge queue when those complete green.

The three out-of-scope findings (#6457, #6458, #6459) are filed and left ungraded for triage. #6457 is the one worth reading first — a user-visible dropped column width on reload, with the grouped path working as both the corroboration and the fix direction.
